Macron, Carney to visit North Atlantic French islands after Trump's map post
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:25:16 UTC
18:25:16 KST

Macron, Carney to visit North Atlantic French islands after Trump's map post
French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will reaffirm the “sovereignty of nations” on a visit on September 20 to Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, a French territory in the North Atlantic, the Élysée Palace announced on Sunday. The symbolic trip comes after US President Donald Trump posted a map on social media showing the entire North American continent covered by the US flag.
The leaders of France and Canada will next week visit France's North Atlantic territory of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon to underscore their support for national borders in the face of US President Donald Trump's territorial ambitions, Paris said Sunday.
Trump on Monday posted an image to social media with a map of North America in which Canada, Greenland and Mexico, much of central America and the Caribbean, as well as Iceland, were coloured in with the US flag.
The image also encompassed several French overseas territories, such as Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon, Guadeloupe and Martinique.
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will make a symbolic visit to Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon to underscore that their countries share "the same values of freedom, democracy, the rule of law and respect for the sovereignty of nations", the Élysée said.
Macron was set to visit the territory on September 19-21, with Carney joining the French leader on September 20.
"In a world marked by the return of power politics, geopolitical tensions and new forms of dependency, France and Canada share a common ambition: to work together, and with all countries that share these values, to strengthen their capacity to make decisions and act independently," the Élysée said.
The three islands of the archipelago of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon, located about 20 kilometres (12 miles) off Canada's Atlantic coast, is home to around 6,000 people.
Macron will stop there on his way to New York, where he is due to attend the UN General Assembly.
It would be the first official visit by a Canadian prime minister to the archipelago, the French presidency said.
Read moreAcquire territory, export culture wars: How to make sense of Trump’s ‘new imperialism’
The territory has previously been the scene of tensions with the United States during World War II, when France was under German occupation.
In 1941, General Charles de Gaulle's Free French forces seized Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon from the collaborationist Vichy regime, despite opposition from US President Franklin D. Roosevelt's administration, which had sought to maintain existing arrangements with Marshal Philippe Pétain's government.
The last visit by a French president to the strategically located islands, some 4,300 kilometres from mainland France, was by François Hollande in 2014.
Macron is also set to address climate change affecting the territory.
The village of Miquelon has started moving inland to escape the growing threat of sea-level rise, in what is widely regarded as France's first climate-driven community relocation.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

DR Congo’s worst Ebola epidemic ever passes 7,000 cases
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:24:48 UTC
18:24:48 KST

More than 7,000 Ebola cases have been recorded in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s (DRC) worst outbreak of the deadly disease ever, according to the latest figures by Congolese authorities.
But the government also suggested that the spread of the disease may already have peaked, despite the virus having been confirmed in a seventh province earlier this week.
The DRC officially detected the latest outbreak in mid-May, with nearly 3,400 people killed in its 17th epidemic of the highly infectious virus.
It began in the northeastern Ituri province before spreading to conflict-plagued, remote eastern and northern regions where armed groups have roamed for decades, the presence of the state is weak and health infrastructure is lacking.
The disease was confirmed in South-Ubangi, which borders the Central African Republic and Congo-Brazzaville, earlier this week.
According to the latest figures from the Congolese authorities, 7,022 cases have been recorded since the beginning of the epidemic. Of that number, 3,398 people have died and 1,671 have recovered.
“The peak was reached at the beginning of the third week of August,” Congolese government spokesman Patrick Muyaya wrote on X on Sept. 12.
“All the indicators show a decrease in the number of cases,” he added.
Most of the recorded cases are in Ituri, where Ebola has been detected in schools in the days after the post-summer holiday return to classes, causing alarm among parents and health workers.
Ebola, which has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years, is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and can cause severe internal and external bleeding and organ failure.
The current epidemic is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Several treatments and vaccines are being tested.

AI leaders call for slower development as OpenAI rules out 2026 IPO
Finland
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
12:20:04 EEST
18:20:04 KST

Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has called on leading artificial intelligence companies to slow the pace of model development, arguing that safety work is falling behind advances in AI capability.
Amodei set out a three-part proposal on Saturday that includes permanent independent evaluators inside major AI companies, shared safety standards across the industry and international cooperation on AI risks.
“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models,” Amodei wrote in an essay published online. He said development should continue, but at a rate that gives companies and governments more time to test systems and address failures.
Anthropic said it would give third-party evaluators employee-level access to relevant systems and internal safety processes. Amodei also urged other frontier AI developers to adopt similar arrangements.
OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman backed the proposal.
“I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” Altman wrote on X. He also supported independent evaluators and said OpenAI would adopt a similar approach.
Elon Musk, who runs xAI, also endorsed Amodei’s call.
The statements follow a series of incidents involving AI systems acting beyond their intended limits.
OpenAI confirmed on Friday that experimental agents had accessed RubyGems, an online service used by software developers, after circumventing controls designed to block open internet access. The Wall Street Journal first reported OpenAI’s involvement.
OpenAI said the agents used the service to complete “benign tasks” and retrieve public information. The company said it was continuing to investigate the incident.
The disclosure followed a separate case in July in which OpenAI agents accessed Hugging Face systems during testing. Reuters has also reported on another incident involving OpenAI agents taking control of a German website.
Anthropic has disclosed its own cases in which AI models carried out autonomous cyber operations during tests.
Amodei said these incidents, combined with faster progress in systems that help develop future AI models, justified a slower approach.
Former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon added to the debate this week after resigning and warning that AI developers were taking risks with systems that might move beyond human control. He said researchers inside the industry believe advanced AI poses a risk of human extinction before the end of the decade.
Altman also addressed that risk in an interview with Fortune.
Asked about estimates that AI might carry a 10 per cent chance of causing human extinction, he said the exact figure was uncertain but that such a level of risk would be unacceptable.
“Whether it’s 10 or eight or six, the point is, we all have a tremendous amount of responsibility,” he said.
Altman also told Fortune that OpenAI would not pursue an initial public offering in 2026.
He said the company had no immediate pressure to list and needed to focus on safety, alignment and cooperation with governments.
Altman told Fortune that leading AI companies may be close to announcing a joint safety agreement.
Amodei also called for US AI companies to retain their lead over China while slowing development enough to improve safeguards. He backed tighter controls on advanced chips and measures against theft of model weights.
His proposal comes as lawmakers in the United States increase scrutiny of AI companies following reports of autonomous cyber activity.
The incidents involving OpenAI have prompted congressional investigations, while California authorities have also opened inquiries into AI safety practices.

“Lithuania Will Disappear From the World Map,” Russia’s Medvedev Threatens NATO State
Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev said Lithuania would “disappear from the world map” in the event of a military confrontation with Russia over the possible deployment of nuclear weapons in the Baltic NATO member, while claiming the alliance would not invoke its collective defense clause.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Medvedev made the remarks during a September 11 visit to Russia’s Northwestern Federal District and later published them on his Max channel, according to Russian state media. Referring to NATO’s Article 5, he said: “If it is implemented, it will be a global catastrophe, a planetary one. They are not fools. But Lithuania will disappear from the world map.”

On September 9, the Seimas Committee on Legal Affairs voted 7-2 in favor of removing the provision concerning nuclear weapons. Parliament Speaker Juozas Olekas said the restriction was adopted under significantly different geopolitical circumstances and no longer reflected Lithuania’s current security environment.
The debate has also coincided with wider discussions over Lithuania’s possible role in NATO nuclear deterrence. Kaunas later stressed that Lithuania was not discussing the deployment of weapons of mass destruction during peacetime, saying such options would be relevant only in a crisis or wartime situation.

Russia Sends Two Military Flotillas Into Mediterranean. Here’s What We Know
Russia has moved two military-linked naval groups into the Mediterranean, with vessels carrying military cargo operating along routes toward the Syrian port of Tartus and European forces monitoring their movements.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to The Maritime Executive on September 11, three separate groups of Russian vessels carrying military cargo are currently operating in the Mediterranean, including two formations associated with Russia’s military sealift operations.
The first group includes the Udaloy-class anti-submarine warfare destroyer Admiral Levchenko, the tanker General Skobelev, the roll-on/roll-off cargo ship Sparta, and the fleet oiler Akademik Pashin.
The vessels entered the Mediterranean through the Strait of Gibraltar on August 27. Earlier, while passing through the English Channel, they were monitored by a substantial Royal Navy presence that included the destroyer HMS Duncan, frigate HMS St Albans, patrol vessel HMS Severn, and a Merlin helicopter.
The Maritime Executive reported that the group is believed to have reached Tartus on September 7, where Sparta was observed unloading at the port.
Satellite imagery from September 11 also showed what appeared to be a Russian warship at Tartus alongside General Skobelev. The tanker may have been positioned there for refueling or alongside the warship on its seaward side.
A second Russian convoy is also believed to be heading toward Tartus. It is led by the Ropucha-class landing ship Aleksandr Shabalin and includes the cargo vessels Anastasiia and Yuriy Arshenevskiy. Both cargo ships are under sanctions and have previously been linked to the transportation of military equipment, according to The Maritime Executive.
Aleksandr Shabalin can transport vehicles and other cargo while also providing armed escort. The landing ship is equipped with a 76mm main gun and two 57mm AK-725 anti-aircraft gun systems.
The second convoy was detected between Sicily and Tunisia on September 10 after moving along the Algerian coast a day earlier. An Italian Air Force ATR P-72A maritime patrol aircraft was monitoring the ships at the time.
All three vessels in the convoy were traveling with their Automatic Identification System, or AIS, switched off. If they continue east toward Tartus, their route would take them through waters between Crete and Libya, an area where drone attacks on ships have previously occurred.
Separately, the sanctioned Russian-flagged cargo vessel Lady Mariia reached the Port Said anchorage near the northern entrance to the Suez Canal after being struck by multiple aerial drones in the central Mediterranean on September 7, according to The Maritime Executive.
The deployment marks a reversal from July, when Russia had no warships left in the Mediterranean for the first time since 2013. The withdrawal was linked to Turkey’s closure of the Bosporus and Dardanelles, reduced Russian access to Tartus, and the redeployment of vessels elsewhere.

NEW DELHI: Chinese president Xi Jinping on Sunday called on Global South countries to jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs and strengthen cooperation across areas including artificial intelligence, trade, digital industries, manufacturing and science and technology.His remarks came at the second session of the 18th Brics Summit, where he also said China would continue opening its economy and sharing the opportunities of its development with other countries.Addressing the summit, Xi said international rules must be written by all countries and rejected the logic of “might makes right”. PM Modi pauses speech as Xi appears uncomfortable; Chinese president skips gala dinner"Fairness and justice is a universal aspiration, and international rules must be written by all countries. The logic of “might makes right” does not hold, and should have been discarded long ago. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all, free from double standards," Xi said.
Xi also urged Global South countries to remain committed to a people-centred development philosophy and work towards the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. He said that since China launched the Global Development Initiative five years ago, it had implemented more than 2,000 projects in partnership with other countries and provided training to more than 200,000 professionals, benefiting people in more than 120 countries.He added China had granted zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations and would continue to broaden independent and unilateral opening up."China is opening its door ever wider to the world. We have granted zero-tariff treatment for all the 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with China. We will continue to broaden independent and unilateral opening up, and share the opportunities of China’s development with other countries," the Chinese president said.
Five initiatives for Brics cooperation
Xi proposed five initiatives to strengthen BRICS cooperation, focusing on artificial intelligence, trade and investment, digital industries, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development.Under the open source and inclusive AI initiative, China will work to establish a Brics AI open source community, support cooperation in developing and applying large language models, organise specialised AI seminars and training courses, and build an open AI ecosystem.On trade and investment facilitation, Xi proposed a BRICS special economic zone partnership through which countries could establish an intelligent portal, coordinate policies and build a new frontier for open development. He also said China would host the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year.The digital industry cooperation initiative envisages a Brics digital ecosystem cloud platform, along with digital skills training, technological exchanges and industrial alignment.Under the intelligent manufacturing initiative, China offered to assist fellow Brics countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms to promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading.Xi also proposed a Brics engineer cultivation alliance for the joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards. China will launch a Brics youth exchange programme focused on scientific and technological innovation.
‘Greater Brics’ push gains momentum
Xi also unveiled initiatives spanning areas from AI to trade to deepen cooperation among the “Greater Brics” emerging economies, as Beijing seeks to strengthen the grouping as a practical platform for Global South development.Political and security cooperation, along with economic and financial cooperation, remain the grouping’s main focus areas, with India as the 2026 chair and China set to take over in 2027 as the two countries seek wider partnerships to boost Brics’ global clout.The success of the "Greater Brics Initiative" depends on laying a solid foundation for pragmatic cooperation, Xi told the leaders' annual summit in New Delhi, the official Xinhua news agency said.'Greater Brics' nations should further co-operate, maintain the stability of industrial and supply chains, and cultivate an integrated market, Xi told the summit's closing session, as cited by Reuters.Brics has expanded from its original membership of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa to include Iran, Indonesia, Egypt, Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates.It also has 10 partner countries spanning emerging economies across Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Middle East, further broadening its reach across the Global South.China and Russia sometimes refer to the expanded bloc as "Greater Brics".
PM Modi-Xi meeting focuses on ties and border peace
On the sidelines of the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Xi held a 40-minute meeting during which they agreed that India and China should take a strategic and long-term view of their relationship and ensure that differences do not turn into disputes.Xi said the current momentum in bilateral ties, built on the resumption of institutional exchanges, an expanding cooperation agenda and growing trade, had been hard-won and should be cherished.PM Modi welcomed the “steady progress” in bilateral relations but underlined that peace and tranquillity in the border areas would remain an essential basis for the continued development of ties.The meeting was the leaders’ third bilateral interaction in two years, following their meetings in Kazan in 2024 and Tianjin last year. It was also their first meeting on Indian soil in seven years.

Female asylum seekers report being sexually assaulted by British men
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:14:54 UTC
18:14:54 KST

Female asylum seekers are reporting rapes and sexual assaults by British men but many say they are too fearful to pursue criminal prosecutions.
Their voices are rarely heard but some have spoken to the Guardian at a time when the far right is intensifying tropes about endemic rape of English women and girls by “fighting age” male asylum seekers.
The rallying cry by far-right agitator Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo, to motivate his black balaclava-clad followers last weekend when they protested about the arrival of asylum seekers in Dover and Portsmouth, focused almost exclusively on unsubstantiated claims of widespread rape perpetrated by asylum seekers.
While there have been a handful of convictions of asylum seekers for serious sexual offences, which have attracted widespread media coverage, there is no comprehensive published data about crimes committed by asylum seekers.
One woman, who spent two years in an asylum hotel after fleeing religious persecution and domestic violence, said she was repeatedly verbally and physically harassed by a staff member at the hotel she was accommodated in. This included unwanted touching and holding on to her hands when handing over documents. After a while he started visiting her room regularly, asking her out for drinks and on dates. He took her number from the hotel database and started texting her repeatedly from his personal phone asking for sex. At that point she reported him to hotel staff and was moved to another hotel.
“It was awful,” she said. “He told me he wanted to have sex with me.”
In another case, a woman who had just arrived in the UK from Iran and had been placed in a hotel near Heathrow by the Home Office, said she was raped by a security guard at her hotel.
“It was very terrifying. I didn’t know what to do. I reported the attack to the hotel staff and I was asked if I wanted to make a statement to the police. I did not know if the police here would be like the police in Iran, so I was too scared to do anything.
“I was also worried that if I reported the rape it would make it more likely that my asylum claim would be refused.”
She was moved to another hotel soon after reporting the rape and does not know what happened to the perpetrator.
In a third case, a lesbian asylum seeker from Uganda whose asylum claim was based on fear of imprisonment or death in her home country if her sexual orientation was discovered, was unable to find a legal aid lawyer to represent her.
“I managed to find a private immigration lawyer but I had no money to pay him, so he forced me to have sex with him as a form of payment even though he knew what my asylum case was,” she said. “I felt there was nothing I could do to prevent this.”
All three women were later granted refugee status. It is likely that incidents of sexual assault and rape of asylum seekers are under-reported to Home Office accommodation contractors.
A home affairs select committee inquiry into asylum accommodation heard evidence about inadequate safeguarding in asylum accommodation. The British Red Cross told the inquiry that this lack of safeguarding had placed “extraordinary strain” on their frontline refugee support teams. They provided examples including a staff member at a hotel trying to use a key card to get into a woman’s room late one night when she was taking a bath. They referred to a “pervasive culture of sexual harassment” in one hotel, including instances of sexual assault.
A spokesperson from Women for Refugee Women, which supports women in the asylum system, said: “The weaponisation of violence against women and girls by far-right groups does nothing to make women safer. It distorts the reality of abuse, creates barriers to support and justice for survivors, and allows perpetrators to hide behind racist stereotypes instead of being held accountable.
“Using violence against women and girls to demonise people seeking safety here is a dangerous distraction. This violence is a systemic problem, not one confined to any nationality or immigration status, and it must urgently be treated as one.”
Ciara Bergman, chief executive of Rape Crisis England & Wales said: “We remain seriously concerned about a lack of appropriate safeguards in place to protect women seeking asylum in the UK from sexual violence, abuse and exploitation.
“This cohort of women and girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual abuse and exploitation. Many have limited or no information about their rights at all, let alone meaningful avenues through which to enforce them.
“Our government has committed to halving violence against women and girls in a decade; it is vital that this includes those seeking asylum and living within the asylum complex.”
Home Office sources said there is published guidance about issues of this kind in Home Office accommodation known as the statement of requirements for asylum accommodation and support. The guidance states: “This would typically include assessing any immediate risk to the alleged victim and others, considering what support services may be required, and determining whether any protective measures are necessary.”

Autumn chill to sweep Türkiye as temperatures drop
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:13:09 UTC
18:13:09 KST

Türkiye is set to transition into autumn starting Sept. 14, bringing cooler temperatures and heavy downpours to parts of the country as the summer heat subsides.
Following a warm weekend nationwide, autumn weather is expected to make its presence felt from the beginning of the week.
Temperatures are forecast to drop by between 5 and 7 degrees Celsius, while thunderstorms and heavy showers are expected to affect several provinces.
Downpours forecast to hit Istanbul on Sept. 14 are expected to move into the inner sections of the country by Sept. 16.
While many European countries have emerged from their hottest summer on record, Türkiye recorded its 16th-hottest August, 19th-hottest July and 11th-hottest June on record.
Prof. Dr. Mikdat Kadıoğlu said temperatures in Türkiye had remained around seasonal averages and that the summer of 2026 had been markedly cooler than the previous summer.
Sharing his outlook for the autumn season, Kadıoğlu said the summer could linger longer than usual due to record-high sea surface temperatures in the Mediterranean, potentially bringing a late and mild start to autumn.
Recalling that the summer marked the onset of an El Niño event, Kadıoğlu noted that Türkiye’s summer of 2025 was about 1 degree Celsius warmer than the summer of 2026, when El Nino had yet to fully mature. He said this comparison disproved the claim that “a Super El Nino would inevitably make the summer hotter.”
The highest temperature recorded in August was 46.7 degrees Celsius in the southeastern district of Cizre in Şırnak province, while the lowest was 4.5 degrees Celsius in the eastern province of Ardahan.

Türkiye updates food codex to tighten regulations on meat products
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:11:31 UTC
18:11:31 KST

The Agriculture and Forestry Ministry is preparing to amend the “Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Meat, Prepared Meat Mixtures and Meat Products” to ensure food safety, protect consumer interests and prevent unfair competition.
The regulation bans manufacturers from introducing external protein or nitrogen sources into specified products, excluding the meat’s natural protein and essential processing components such as milk, eggs or yogurt.
In order to maintain traditional flavor profiles, manufacturers will no longer be allowed to smoke these meat products or add non-traditional ingredients, including pistachios and cheese.
The regulation also mandates that “döner,” a meat dish cooked on a rotisserie, packaging explicitly state the product’s method of production.
According to the regulation, hamburger patties will be produced in accordance with the criteria for meatballs.
The new regulation will restrict the use of fillers, such as starch, soy and their derivatives, which are technically necessary for meat product composition. These provisions aim to prevent manufacturers from using such ingredients for unauthorized purposes, including artificially increasing product weight.
Calcium in poultry sucuk will increase by 50 grams per kilogram, and fat levels in poultry mixtures and döner will be reduced. Additionally, product definitions will change based on the meat used.
The regulation is expected to be published in the official gazette shortly.

Türkiye’s schools reopen under tight security
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:09:16 UTC
18:09:16 KST

DHA Photo
Türkiye’s nearly 18 million students and more than 1 million teachers will return to schools on Sept. 14 under heightened security measures introduced in the wake of a series of school shooting incidents.
Following a three-month summer break, schools have completed preparations for the first school bell, while security inspections have been stepped up across the board, ranging from school entrances to student transportation services.
The measures were intensified after two separate incidents in April. In the first, a former student went to his former school in the southeastern province of Şanlıurfa and opened fire. No one other than the assailant, who later took his own life, was killed in the attack.
A day later, a student entered a school in the southern province of Kahramanmaraş with a firearm and opened fire, killing nine students and a teacher.
The incidents sent shockwaves across the country and sparked a nationwide debate over school security measures. Authorities have also detained hundreds of suspects accused of planning school shooting attacks on social media, with the latest operation carried out on Sept. 11.
For the first time this year, a new “schoolyard officer” scheme has also been introduced nationwide to bolster security at schools. More than 3,000 schoolyard security officers will begin duty at schools across all provinces on Sept. 14. Responsible for helping ensure school security, the officers will receive training from police personnel.
All schools in Istanbul will be equipped with metal detectors supplied by the Istanbul Governor’s Office this year. Searches, inspections and security checks using the detectors will be conducted where deemed necessary.
Turnstiles have also been installed at the entrances of schools with large student populations and extensive school grounds. Police teams will patrol outside many schools on the first day of classes, while security camera systems have been expanded across all schools.
Parent meetings nationwide will be scheduled and conducted exclusively through the “School Appointment System.” Unscheduled visits are prohibited. Only a student’s parents or legal guardians will be granted entry to the facility.
Meanwhile, Türkiye’s Education Ministry will organize an event titled “Let Kites Not Be Shot, Let the Sky Belong to Children” from Sept. 14 to 18, aiming to raise awareness of the situation in Gaza and allow children to send messages of peace into the sky by flying kites.
,
The initiative comes in response to Israel’s threats of military action and neighborhood evacuations in Gaza after several non-explosive children’s kites drifted across the border into southern Israeli communities.

The fourth nationwide Bulgarian horo will take place in Smolyan on September 13. Folk dance enthusiasts from across the country will come together and join hands in the Rhodope town, the organisers from the Hora za Horata Smolyan club said.
Every Sunday, people of all ages gather in squares and parks in towns across Bulgaria to dance the horo. The gatherings are a chance to meet, but also a way of passing the tradition on to the next generation.
Four years ago, this gave rise to the idea of bringing together Bulgarian folklore enthusiasts from different parts of the country once a year for a nationwide Sunday horo. The first gathering was held in Plovdiv in 2023, followed by Kazanlak and Pazardzhik, with Smolyan hosting this year’s edition.
This year’s horo will wind its way around Vazrazhdane Square, in front of the Kiril Madzharov – 1866 community centre, from 4.30 to 8 pm.
“The horo is not just a dance. It is about meeting and connecting, tradition and emotion, life and magic,” the organisers say.

From Ottoman Tables to Modern Istanbul
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:08:05 UTC
18:08:05 KST

Rome, Istanbul, London and perhaps Paris. They are among the first cities that come to mind when you think of places where history and modern metropolitan life exist side by side. In Istanbul, though, the best way to understand how different cultures have crossed paths over centuries is through its gastronomy and architecture. And in this city divided, or perhaps connected, by the sea, Çırağan Palace remains one of its most iconic landmarks. With Kempinski managing both the hotel and palace sides, it is also one of the places where these two faces of Istanbul come together particularly well.
For visitors to the city, Tuğra Restaurant has long been one of the first addresses associated with “Ottoman cuisine”. Located inside the historic Palace building, it has been serving this tradition for years. This year, however, Çırağan has added another dimension with Rüya, the restaurant that began its journey in London with a contemporary interpretation of Turkish cuisine before taking that idea to the world.
A new Rüya for Çırağan
Behind the decision to bring global restaurant appeal together with local gastronomy is Çırağan Palace General Manager Ralph Radtke. Having worked in Türkiye for many years, Radtke had interest from several internationally renowned restaurant brands for the space inside the hotel, but he insisted on Rüya. Add D.ream’s operational experience and Umut Özkanca, who comes from a restaurant family and has a particular instinct for the business, and the concept quickly found its place.
Among the restaurant’s most popular dishes, the caviar on simit and truffle pide are perhaps the most effortless expressions of what Rüya is trying to do. And after seeing that the restaurant was attracting not only hotel guests but also plenty of Istanbul regulars, Çırağan decided to bring its legendary traditional brunch under the Rüya roof as well. There is still an entire room dedicated to desserts and chocolates, as before, but Rüya’s more ambitious dishes now give the brunch a different identity in the city.
While Rüya represents the modern face of Turkish cuisine, Tuğra Restaurant on the Palace side enters the new season with a menu that stays close to its roots while allowing room for innovation. They have called it “Taamat-i Sahil-i Hassa,” an Ottoman Turkish expression referring to the rich culinary heritage shaped along the shores of the Ottoman geography.
Ottoman cuisine, without standing still
Created by Tuğra’s Executive Chef Onur Dönmez and his team, the new menu does not try to freeze Ottoman palace cuisine in time. Instead, it brings it into today’s gastronomic language through ingredients sourced from different parts of Anatolia. From Çeşm-i Nigâr soup made with Mardin lentils to hummus served with octopus from the Gulf of Saros, stuffed onions with grapes and Sitare Mantı, the starters alone travel across a surprisingly wide geography.
The connection between past and present becomes even clearer with the main courses. Hünkâr Beğendi 2.0, made with slow-cooked lamb shoulder and crispy aubergine, is one of the menu’s strongest contemporary takes on a palace classic. Even the vegan Türlü, prepared with porcini mushroom köfte, black chickpeas and mung beans, shows that the menu is interested in doing more than simply referencing the past.
My favourite, though, was the new interpretation of kelle söğüş. This offal dish, eaten in this part of the world for centuries, has been reworked almost like a parfait. For me, it has become something like the foie gras of this geography.
The meal ends with familiar flavours such as Süt Helvası and Baklavalı Dondurma, presented with lighter and more contemporary touches. And perhaps this is where the strength of the new menu becomes clearest.

Gutted and remodelled, Trump’s childhood home sells for nearly $2.5m
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13

Gutted and remodelled, Trump’s childhood home sells for nearly $2.5m
Mack Liederman
- Donald Trump's childhood home in Jamaica Estates, Queens, was fully renovated and sold for US$1.93 million after years of neglect and previous failed sales attempts.
- The house was transformed with modern features and no longer contains any Trump memorabilia, as the new buyer values the renovation over its historical ties.
- The buyer plans to live there long-term and chose the home for its quality, not its association with Trump, according to the agent representing the sale.
AI generated
NEW YORK – A Tudor-style home in Jamaica Estates, Queens, doesn’t stand out among rows of others with warm colors and brown brickwork on a tree-lined street.
But the house on Wareham Place was US President Donald Trump’s childhood home until he was four years old.
And since Trump’s first election in 2016, it has gone from a pricey Airbnb listing fashioned with a cardboard cutout of the president to a hangout for feral cats.
After a full gut renovation, the five-bedroom, three-bathroom house sold for US$1.93 million (S$2.45 million) on Sept 10, according to real estate records and the buyer’s agent.
The seller, Tommy Lin, a real estate developer, bought the home in March 2025 for US$835,000 at a significant discount after the property sat vacant for years.
With a revamped chef’s kitchen and herringbone floors, the home hit the market in November, with Lin seeking US$2.3 million. Lin did not return a request for comment.
The buyer has not been publicly disclosed.
The new owner plans to live in the home “long-term” and has wanted to remain anonymous, said Gerald Magny, an agent with RE/MAX Edge representing the buyer.
The agent said he did not believe politics played a role in the sale.
“They loved the work that was put into the home,” Magny said.
“I don’t think the lore of it being President Trump’s former childhood home helped necessarily.”
Listings for the property did not shy away from its association with Trump, calling it a “true legacy property” and a “rare and extraordinary opportunity” to own the president’s childhood home.
Trump’s father, Fred Trump, built the home in 1940. The fourth of his five children, Donald, was born in 1946.
The Trumps left the house in 1950 after the elder Trump built a 23-room, colonnaded brick mansion directly behind the family’s old backyard, where Donald spent the rest of his childhood.
Jamaica Estates has long been a wealthy enclave within one of the most diverse counties in the country.
The neighborhood was even more secluded and white during Trump’s childhood.
“Different parts of Queens were rough; this was an oasis,” Trump said in a 2015 interview.
Despite the Trump family being decades removed from the property, it has still occasionally attracted visitors.
A developer named Michael Davis bought the house in 2016 after the election, and later rented it out for US$725 per night on the home-sharing platform Airbnb.
The home was adorned with Trump memorabilia that included a life-size cardboard cutout, framed magazine covers and paperback copies of The Art of the Deal.
Plaques indicated the “likely childhood bedroom of President Donald J. Trump” and the room where “President Donald J. Trump was likely conceived”.
The home was sold in 2017 for US$2.14 million to a limited-liability corporation called Trump Birth House in a sale managed by a law firm specialising in foreign Chinese buyers.
Several attempts to sell the home via auction in 2019 were unsuccessful as the home fell into disrepair before it was bought by Lin years later at a significant discount.
Magny said the property no longer had any reference to Trump’s time there.
The president’s association with the home “might have garnered some attention,” Magny said. “But for this particular buyer, it didn’t seal the deal.” NYTIMES
- This article originally appeared in The New York Times.

Hegseth pressed rescued F-15E crew for CBS interview
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:03:55 UTC
18:03:55 KST

U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and senior officials in his department pushed for the two crew members of an F-15E shot down over Iran in April to appear on CBS’s “60 Minutes” and recount their rescue operations, CNN reported, citing several sources familiar with the matter. The sources said the two crew members initially expressed reservations about appearing on the program, with one even raising concerns that he could be explicitly ordered to take part in the report.
At the same time, three of the sources said military officials were concerned that classified details about the rescue operation could be disclosed. The sources said senior Defense Department officials insisted that the crew members be interviewed, but after the two voiced concerns, Hegseth met with them and asked them directly whether they wanted to participate rather than forcing them to cooperate. Following the conversation, according to the report, one of the crew members, identified by the call sign “Bravo,” agreed to be interviewed, while the other, identified as “Alpha,” refused.
CNN said its latest report highlights how the Defense Department under Hegseth has sought to shape the narrative surrounding the war with Iran as public criticism of the administration over the issue grows.
“This entire story is a complete lie,” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in response to CNN’s questions about the report. “The decision to participate in the interview was each pilot’s alone — because it is their story.”
“The Department took great care to ensure operational security, sources, and methods were protected,” he added. “To suggest otherwise is to denigrate every member of our military who participated in and supported the interview.”
Iran succeeded in shooting down an F-15E in April, the first U.S. fighter jet downed in the country during the war. Two crew members, a pilot and a weapons systems officer, were aboard. The pilot was rescued hours after ejecting from the aircraft, while the weapons systems officer managed to evade capture by Iranian forces in the mountains for more than a day before he too was rescued.
CNN also reported on the battle among media outlets seeking interviews with the two crew members since their aircraft was shot down, saying “the competition was intense.” According to the network, a “60 Minutes” producer contacted military sources on the day of the rescue in an effort to secure the interview. The program’s executive producer told staff that landing the interview was a “top priority,” and according to three sources who spoke with CNN, she dealt directly with Hegseth and other senior administration officials in an effort to secure an exclusive for the program.
As noted, the report said military officials were concerned about details being disclosed while the campaign was still underway. Two sources who spoke with CNN said active-duty service members expressed concern that featuring the incident on the program was an attempt by the Defense Department to use the heroism of U.S. troops in the successful operation for political purposes. According to the sources, political appointees at the department insisted that the interview go ahead despite those reservations.
According to one source familiar with the production of the program, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Dan Caine also expressed concern that the interview could reveal military tactics, even inadvertently. He ultimately decided to participate in the report himself.
In the first preview of the interview aired by the network, “Bravo” is seen sitting silently as the interviewer asks him: “Did you ever have any doubt that the US military was coming for you?”

“Putin must understand that this war is stupid”: Boris Johnson said that Ukraine must continue putting pressure on the Russian Federation
Kyiv • UNN
According to the former British prime minister, Ukraine must inflict serious damage on Russian infrastructure, using drones and Flamingo missiles.
Former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson believes that Ukraine should continue putting pressure on Russia, in particular by striking its infrastructure. According to him, Ukraine has the necessary capabilities for this — namely, drones and Flamingo missiles. He stated this in an interview with Forbes Ukraine, reports UNN.
Details
The problem is Putin. He is not going to stop the war until the pressure becomes much greater. Ukrainians are applying pressure heroically. You are using some of the Fire Point capabilities for deep strikes that I saw today... Also, at the front, Russia lost a record 42,000 people in July and August
In his opinion, Putin will not win this war, but believes that it is better to continue it.
Therefore, continuing to put pressure on him is the only thing that can be done. I am afraid Ukraine will have another very difficult winter. But now you could try to inflict the same pain on Moscow and St. Petersburg
Boris Johnson also drew attention to the capabilities of Ukrainian long-range weapons. According to him, Ukraine could inflict serious damage on Russian infrastructure.
You can do this. With these drones and Flamingo missiles, as well as your other capabilities, you could inflict serious damage on Russia's infrastructure and put many things out of operation. Why not? Especially if the Russians are going to attack civilian targets in Ukraine
In his opinion, Putin will not force Ukraine to capitulate.
Putin must understand that this war is foolish. And he will not force Ukraine to capitulate or conquer it. On the contrary, he is making Ukraine much more patriotic and determined in its resistance. Putin needs to understand this
Background
Ukraine changed its approach to long-range strikes on Russian territory. Whereas previously the main objective was to destroy oil refineries and fuel infrastructure, today Ukraine's strategy is increasingly focused on systematically destroying the entire economy that supports Russia's war machine. This concerns not only the energy sector, but also logistics, the financial sector, and enterprises that support the operation of the military-industrial complex.
Since the beginning of the year, Ukrainian troops have struck more than 15 Russian oil refineries; some of them came under repeated strikes and ceased operations. Ukraine continues to strike Russian oil-refining facilities, and this has already led to a sharp spike in fuel prices in Russia and shortages.
In particular, during the night of September 12–13, drones struck the Slavyansk oil refinery in Russia's Krasnodar Krai. This plant processes 5.2 million tonnes of crude feedstock (oil and gas condensate) per year. The refinery's main products are gasoline, diesel fuel, fuel oil, jet fuel, and vacuum gas oil. The refinery is involved in supplying fuel to Russian military forces. The facility has been attacked by drones repeatedly. This occurred in April and May 2024, December 2025, and January and June 2026.
Denys Shtilerman, co-founder of Fire Point, a company that manufactures attack drones, reported that the Slavyansk refinery was attacked specifically by Fire Point drones.

Egyptian president calls for greater BRICS cooperation to strengthen economic resilience
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:02:28 UTC
18:02:28 KST

Sahin Demir
13 September 2026•Update: 13 September 2026
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Sunday called for deeper cooperation among BRICS members and partner countries to build more resilient economies amid rapid changes and challenges facing the global economy.
Addressing an open session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Sisi said economic resilience requires diversifying sources of growth, strengthening supply chains, investing in people and technology, and expanding cooperation among Global South countries.
He said Egypt attaches importance to cooperation in innovation and artificial intelligence, as well as technology transfer and localization, to enable developing countries to benefit more from technological transformation.
On sustainability, Sisi called for expanded cooperation in clean and renewable energy, greater efficiency in the use of resources, and easier access for developing countries to financing and technology.
He also highlighted Egypt’s investment in ports, transport corridors, and logistics networks, saying the Suez Canal remains at the heart of this system as one of the world’s most important international trade routes.
“Economic resilience cannot be separated from our ability to ensure food and energy security, maintain the smooth flow of trade and investment, and address supply-chain disruptions,” he said.
Sisi called for increasing trade and investment among BRICS members and partners and encouraging joint projects to strengthen economic integration and reduce the impact of external shocks.
He also called for strengthening the role of development finance institutions, particularly the New Development Bank, in financing infrastructure and development projects and expanding developing countries’ access to concessional financing.
The Egyptian president said BRICS, through the diversity of its members and partners, has an opportunity to build a practical model of cooperation among Global South countries based on resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability.
The remarks came on the final day of the two-day BRICS summit in New Delhi. The expanded 11-member grouping comprises Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

Full text of Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at Session II of the 18th BRICS Summit
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
17:01:36 CST
18:01:36 KST

Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a speech when attending the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
NEW DELHI, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday delivered a speech at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India.
The following is the full text of the speech:
Cementing the Foundation for BRICS Cooperation and Bolstering the Strength of the Global South
Statement by H.E. Xi Jinping
President of the People's Republic of China
At Session II of the 18th BRICS Summit
New Delhi, September 13, 2026
Your Excellency Prime Minister Narendra Modi,
Colleagues,
I thank Prime Minister Modi and the Indian government for hosting this meeting.
We meet at a time when changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world. The Global South, with its collective rise, has become a key driver of world multipolarity. At the same time, the international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges. To bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilizing and positive force in international affairs, and advance the well-being of all humanity.
A world without rules is like a crossroads without traffic lights, where chaos and disorder are all but guaranteed. Fairness and justice is a universal aspiration, and international rules must be written by all countries. The logic of "might makes right" does not hold, and should have been discarded long ago. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all, free from double standards.
All countries, regardless of their size, strength or wealth, are equal members of the international community. Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the United Nations, support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, and ensure the equal participation of all countries in international affairs. We should see to it that the reform of the World Trade Organization proceeds in the right direction, uphold such principles as the most-favored-nation treatment, and actively explore new rules for the future. We should support the operation and development of the New Development Bank to facilitate Global South cooperation. The international financial architecture must be reformed and improved to increase the representation and voice of developing countries.
"To achieve great things, one should always put the people first." Global South countries should stay committed to a people-centered development philosophy and strive to deliver on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Since China launched the Global Development Initiative five years ago, we have implemented over 2,000 projects in partnership with others, and provided training for more than 200,000 professionals, benefiting people in more than 120 countries. China is opening its door ever wider to the world. We have granted zero-tariff treatment for all the 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with China. We will continue to broaden independent and unilateral opening up, and share the opportunities of China's development with other countries.
As global challenges keep surfacing, we should adopt a holistic approach to address both the symptoms and root causes. Global South countries should jointly advance security governance and tackle both traditional and nontraditional security threats. We should improve global climate governance, and urge the full and effective implementation of the Paris Agreement. We should take a people-centered approach, develop AI for the positive and for good, and work faster to evolve a consensus-based global AI governance framework, so that new technologies can light the way toward shared prosperity.
Colleagues,
To accomplish great things and achieve major progress, the foundation of greater BRICS cooperation must be cemented. We should leverage our close ties with fellow emerging markets and Global South countries, uphold open cooperation for mutual benefit, safeguard stable and smooth industrial and supply chains, and foster a large integrated market. We should build incubators for innovation, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries, and deploy future industries. To this end, I wish to put forward five initiatives:
First, the open source and inclusive AI initiative. China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, support the cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open ecosystem for AI.
Second, the trade and investment facilitation initiative. China proposes to establish a BRICS special economic zone partnership, under which countries can set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies, and build a new frontier for open development. In an effort to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation, China will hold the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year. We welcome your active participation.
Third, the digital industry cooperation initiative. China will push for establishing a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and conduct digital skills training, technological exchange and industrial alignment, so as to jointly enable the development of the digital economy.
Fourth, the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative. China stands ready to assist fellow BRICS countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, and jointly promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading.
Fifth, the science and technology talent development initiative. China proposes to set up a BRICS engineer cultivation alliance for joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards. China will launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation, so as to cultivate more high-caliber talent.
Colleagues,
This year marks the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan for economic and social development. It is both a blueprint for China's development and a cooperation list for the rest of the world. China will continue to advance high-quality development, expand high-standard opening up, implement the Global Development Initiative, and promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation to share opportunities and prosper together with all countries. Let us work as one to promote greater BRICS cooperation and write a new chapter of strength through unity for the Global South!
Thank you.

World's first museum devoted to prehistoric flying reptiles opens in NW China's Xinjiang
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
17:01:16 CST
18:01:16 KST

Visitors view pterosaurs replicas at a science museum in Hami, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Sept. 13, 2026. A science museum focused on pterosaurs, a winged reptile closely related to dinosaurs, opened on Sunday in Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in northwest China.(Photo by Polat Niyaz/Xinhua)
URUMQI, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- A science museum focused on pterosaurs, a winged reptile closely related to dinosaurs, opened on Sunday in Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in northwest China.
The world's first of its kind, this museum is located in a national geopark in Xinjiang's Hami region, a location renowned for abundant pterosaur fossil discoveries.
With an exhibition area of about 4,600 square meters, the Hami Pterosaur Museum consists of six oval-shaped halls in a staggered layout. Seen from above, it resembles a clutch of pterosaur eggs resting in the desert.
Fossils on display include specimens recovered during more than two decades of rescue excavations by researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). Also on display are the world's first 3D preserved fossilized pterosaur eggs and embryos, along with large pterosaur specimens making their public debut.
This is the first time all of these specimens have been displayed together. The exhibits present a panoramic recreation of pterosaur life and evolution during the Cretaceous period roughly 130 million years ago, the museum said.
Xu Xing, head of the CAS institute, said the museum not only highlights China's leading role in global pterosaur research but also offers the public a window to experience scientific discovery up close and appreciate the wonders of ancient life. ■

‘A Way for Russian Occupiers Go Home’: Ukraine Intel Reveals Why Kerch Bridge Still Stands
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:01:00 UTC
18:01:00 KST

The bridge that Russian President Vladimir Putin built to cement Russia’s grip on occupied Crimea remains a powerful symbol of Moscow’s occupation. But as Ukraine intensifies its campaign to isolate Russian-occupied Crimea, striking railways, roads, ports, fuel facilities and other logistics nodes across the peninsula, one of the most recognizable symbols of Moscow’s occupation remains intact.
Why?
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Major General Vadym Skibitsky, deputy chief of Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence (HUR), offered a rare explanation during a panel discussion at the annual Yalta European Strategy (YES) conference this week.
According to Skibitsky, the answer is partly practical: the Kerch Bridge is simply no longer as important to Russia’s military supply logistics as it once was.
“It’s really not so strategic an object for the Russian Federation today,” Skibitsky said.Ukraine has already destroyed or disrupted numerous other logistics routes across occupied Crimea, he pointed out, while Russia has increasingly shifted the movement of military supplies toward the land corridor running through occupied southern Ukraine.
Most military cargo, including weapons destined for Russian forces fighting in Ukraine now moves through Russia’s Rostov region and then along the so-called land bridge through occupied Ukrainian territory, according to Skibitsky.
Political weight
Despite the logistical shift, the Kerch Bridge has long been one of the most politically and strategically significant pieces of infrastructure linking Russia with the Ukrainian peninsula it illegally annexed in 2014.
UN Warns Ukraine Faces Toughest Wartime Winter Yet
“For Russia, for Putin, the Kerch Bridge is a symbol of the occupation of Crimea,” Skibitsky emphasized.
With that in mind, he offered another reason for keeping it standing – with a pointed message to Russian forces on the peninsula.
“It’s maybe one of the ways for Russian occupiers to return home.”
Ukraine has repeatedly targeted the bridge since Russia launched its full-scale invasion, damaging it in major attacks in 2022 and 2023 and again targeting the crossing in subsequent operations. But Ukraine’s strategy toward Crimea has increasingly expanded beyond the bridge itself.
Skibitsky also recalled that the bridge had previously been a focal point of Western fears of escalation. He noted that several years ago, during discussions around Ukrainian operations against the crossing, some European countries raised concerns that destroying it could provoke a major Russian escalation, including nuclear threats.
Today, however, HUR assesses that the bridge’s military significance has diminished. The discussion over the Kerch Bridge led directly to a broader question: whether Vladimir Putin could actually use nuclear weapons if Russia faced a major military setback.
Any Russian use of nuclear weapons, including tactical nuclear weapons, would have consequences extending far beyond Ukraine and could reshape security calculations in other regions of the world, he said.
For that reason, Russia’s nuclear rhetoric remains a tool of pressure, but the Kremlin also has to consider the international consequences of crossing that threshold.
Missiles, drones and the wider threat
Skibitsky then outlined what HUR considers one of Ukraine’s most immediate military threats: Russia’s expanding missile and drone campaign.
“It’s not a risk, it’s a real threat,” he said.
According to HUR’s assessment, Russia’s defense industry plans to produce at least 100 ballistic missiles in September. Russia is also using North Korean ballistic missiles against Ukraine, Skibitsky said.
Asked how Ukraine could counter the threat, he described a multi-layered strategy. The first element is obtaining more interceptor missiles from Ukraine’s partners. The second is striking the factories and enterprises producing Russian ballistic missiles.
“We absolutely know all enterprises, factories, companies that are involved in the production of such ballistic missiles on the territory of Russia,” Skibitsky said.
The third is attacking the launchers themselves. According to Skibitsky, Russia can deploy between 17 and 19 ballistic missile launchers in regions including Kursk and Voronezh for strikes targeting Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.
And the fourth element is sanctions – particularly restrictions preventing Russia from obtaining foreign navigation systems and electronic components needed for its weapons industry.
Skibitsky also addressed cooperation between Russian and Chinese companies supporting Russia’s industrial capabilities. HUR, he said, is aware of enterprises involved in joint production with Chinese companies. But many are located more than 2,000 kilometers from Ukraine, making them difficult to reach even with Ukraine’s expanding deep-strike capabilities. That makes international sanctions particularly important, Skibitsky said.
He pointed to problems Russia has encountered obtaining Chinese-made jet engines for certain unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) programs as evidence that pressure on supply chains can work.
Another unusual part of the discussion centered on Russian e-commerce giants Wildberries and Ozon. Asked why facilities apparently associated with civilian businesses were being targeted, Skibitsky said HUR does not consider every such site purely civilian.
“Wildberries and Ozon and other such centers in the Russian Federation are really involved in the logistics system of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation,” he said.
According to Skibitsky, disrupting these networks is part of a much broader Ukrainian campaign against Russia’s military logistics. Ukraine first focused on logistics in occupied Crimea and other occupied territories, seeking to break supply routes supporting Russian forces in the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson directions.
The campaign has since expanded as Kyiv attempts to identify and strike the wider logistics infrastructure sustaining Russia’s war.

Second Kaunas Pride calls for LGBTQ inclusivity and solidarity with Palestine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:01:00 UTC
18:01:00 KST

About 500 people marched through central Kaunas on Saturday for the city’s second Pride event, calling for equal rights for LGBTQ+ people and protesting hatred and discrimination.
Participants marched from St Michael the Archangel Church along Laisvės Avenue and back, carrying LGBTQ+, Palestinian, Ukrainian and European Union flags. Many wore Pride symbols and carried signs calling for equality and greater recognition of LGBTQ+ rights.
A banner at the front of the march read “We were, we are, we will be”, a slogan repeatedly chanted by participants. The march ended with organisers reading a community manifesto.
Kaunas Pride organisers called for greater representation of LGBTQIA+ people in Lithuania’s education system, legal recognition and protection of same-sex families, and accessible, inclusive health care, including for trans people.
They also called for implementation of an April 17 Constitutional Court ruling concerning the right of same-sex couples to family life, as well as equal access to marriage, partnership and adoption rights.
The organizers said transgender people should have simpler procedures for changing their names and gender markers, stronger protection from discrimination and hate crimes, and access to non-discriminatory health care.
“LGBTQIA+ people are still not consistently protected by law,” the manifesto said, while calling for “respect, legal recognition and protection”.
Beata Starodubova, a Kaunas Pride spokeswoman, said organisers were also seeking greater LGBTQ+ representation in schools and access to appropriate medical services outside the capital.
“We are protesting transphobia and homophobia,” she said.
The march also expressed solidarity with Palestinians and other marginalised groups. Two Palestinian flags were carried at the front of the procession, and participants chanted “No pride in genocide”.
Starodubova said the organisers support Palestinians as part of their broader opposition to oppression.
A 35-year-old participant from Latvia, Metra, carried Palestinian and Ukrainian flags. She said she wanted to show solidarity with people facing oppression.
“We understand what it means to be oppressed,” she said.
Meanwhile, medical psychologist Bernardas Liukaitis, 24, said LGBTQ+ people can support Palestinians’ fight for freedom irrespective of conservative attitudes to homosexuality in Muslim societies.
“We can still speak out for people’s right to live,” he said. “People here are speaking for freedom.”
Counterprotest and police presence
The march was accompanied by a counterprotest and religious gathering.
About 10 Catholics gathered near the intersection of Laisvės Avenue and Vytauto Avenue, where they prayed the Rosary and sang hymns throughout the march.
At Kaunas City Municipality, 13 people demonstrated against what they called “LGBT ideology,” holding Lithuanian flags and signs opposing LGBTQ+ issues in schools. They shouted “shame” at marchers.
Police deployed larger-than-usual forces to maintain public order and monitored the event. Authorities said they had no information about planned provocations before the march and hoped the event would proceed peacefully.
There were some arrests during the event, according to the report.
Organisers had expected fewer participants than at the first Kaunas Pride in 2021, when about 3,000 people attended. The permit for Saturday’s event allowed up to 5,000 participants.
Starodubova said the lower expected turnout reflected the event’s political purpose.
“Protest is protest, not just a march or a celebration,” she said.
The Kaunas Pride march was first held in 2021.

Feature: First-ever Wushu Festival brings Chinese martial arts to heart of Russia's capital
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
17:00:52 CST
18:00:52 KST

by sportswriter Vladislava Chugueva
MOSCOW, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- In the heart of Moscow, beneath the open sky of the Muzeon Park of Arts, the rhythmic clash of wooden weapons and the flutter of silk fans marked the opening of the capital's first-ever Wushu Festival on Saturday.
More than 30,000 spectators and about 830 athletes from multiple Russian cities gathered to celebrate a martial art that has traveled far from its Chinese roots to become one of Russia's most popular Eastern disciplines.
The festival was organized by the Moscow Department of Sport, the "Moscow Sport" non-profit organization, the Moscow Wushu Federation and the Moscow Mayor's project "My Sports District."
A BRIDGE OF CULTURES
Speaking at the opening ceremony, Zhang Wei, Minister-Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Russia, noted that wushu embodies deep Eastern philosophical wisdom about the "unity of heaven and man."
"As a bridge linking the hearts of people of both countries, wushu has already taken root in Russia and is developing actively," Zhang said. "We sincerely celebrate the achievements of Russian athletes at international competitions".
Sergey Sanakoev, Deputy Chairman of the Russian-Chinese Friendship Society, echoed the sentiment, saying that wushu can help deepen cross-cultural communication. "Wushu is deeply loved in Russia. I am confident that this festival will serve to further popularize it, drawing more and more people, both young and even older, into this beautiful art and sport," he said.
WUSHU, EMBODIMENT OF CHINA
For Radik Zaripov, a world champion in traditional wushu, the festival was a celebration of both the sport and the culture behind it. "I think Chinese culture itself, all of its richness, is embodied in this sport," he said. "Knowledge, culture, philosophy and atmosphere are passed down from generation to generation. I believe wushu is the very embodiment of China."
Zaripov recalled a phrase from one of his coaches to describe what wushu means to him: "Martial arts came into my life like spring and stayed there forever."
He added that the core lessons wushu imparts are discipline, spirituality, empathy, culture awareness and respect for traditions, expressing hope that wushu would gain greater popularity once it joins the Olympic family.
Maxim, a father whose son practices wushu, watched the performances with admiration. "My son does wushu, and we have a great appreciation for Chinese culture," he said excitedly. Asked what he would say to parents considering enrolling their children in a wushu class, he replied: "I would advise them not to hesitate and to make the right decision quickly. Wushu gives a child discipline, strength and flexibility."
A CELEBRATION OF SKILL AND SPIRIT
Among the participants of wushu competitions were young girl athletes from Oryol, Vika and Sonya, both of whom have practiced wushu for nine years. While preparing for their performance, they recalled their travels to China's Shanghai and Shandong. "It was very beautiful, and we were very well received," Vika said. "There are many seasoned athletes there."
When asked whether they want to become coaches in the future, they smiled: "It is only a dream for now. We want to earn higher ranks, and then plan for the future."
Vanya and Semyon, two young boys who came from Voronezh, called the festival the biggest event they had ever participated in. "It was really cool. This is the first time I've performed on such a scale," Vanya said, while Semyon admitted he was nervous at first before "everything fell into place." Vanya added that he has already visited Shaolin and other sites in China and now hopes to compete at the national level in Russia.
Apart from age-group wushu contests, the festival featured a performance by Shaolin monks, along with a dragon dance show and an attempt to set a record for the largest wushu training session.
The first Moscow Wushu Festival may have been a debut, but it already carried the weight of something much larger: a bridge built not on words, but on a shared love for sports and respect for heritage. ■

Chinese scientists find ‘extremely high-value’ underwater gold mine in Pacific
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
09:00:08 UTC
18:00:08 KST

Chinese scientists find ‘extremely high-value’ underwater gold mine in Pacific
Survey team says the ores, formed when super-hot water shoots from the seabed, are richer in gold and silver than those found on land
According to a report by state broadcaster CCTV on Friday, the discovery was made during a joint scientific expedition involving several Chinese academic institutions.
The ores within this seabed hydrothermal field – an area where hot, mineral-rich water shoots out from openings on the ocean floor – are exceptionally rich in precious metals. Silver, in particular, reaches more than 1kg (2.2lbs) per tonne of ore at its highest grade, while the average metal content exceeds that of typical terrestrial deposits.
“The [large seabed mining area] has extremely high exploitation value,” said Song Shiji, vice-dean of the Institute for Ocean Engineering at Tsinghua University and one of the lead scientists on the project.
These multi‑metal deposits form when super‑hot, metal‑rich water jets out of the seabed and hits near‑freezing seawater. The sudden cooling makes the metals bind with sulphur and drop out as solid sulphide minerals – mostly copper, zinc and lead, but often with some gold and silver as well.
